label: Person
name: Albert Onyembo Lomandjo
summary:
Albert Onyembo Lomandjo (b. 1947) is a Congolese Catholic bishop who has served in the Democratic Republic of Congo, one of Africa's most Catholic countries and one of its most tragically war-torn. Born in Congo (then Belgian Congo), he was ordained a priest and consecrated bishop in one of the world's largest Catholic national communities.

The DRC has one of the world's largest Catholic populations—estimated at 40% of the country's 100+ million people—and its bishops wield exceptional moral authority in a country where the state has repeatedly failed to provide justice, security, or development. The National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) has been one of the most politically significant Catholic bodies in Africa, mediating between warring factions, monitoring elections, and demanding governmental accountability.

Onyembo Lomandjo's episcopal ministry has been conducted against the backdrop of extraordinary violence: Mobutu's kleptocracy, the two Congo Wars of the late 1990s and early 2000s, the ongoing conflict in the eastern Congo that has claimed millions of lives, and the systemic poverty of a country whose mineral wealth has funded devastating proxy wars. Congolese Catholic bishops have provided some of the most courageous witness to human rights in contemporary African history.
